case_title: Raja Gounder & Anr. v. State of Tamil Nadu
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were brothers involved in a land dispute, which created strained relations. The incident occurred at night, and the victim was attacked. The first informant, who was the wife of the victim and sister-in-law of the accused, reported the incident after a delay. The post-mortem revealed more injuries than initially mentioned in the FIR. The courts below examined the delay in lodging the FIR, the absence of an independent witness, and the discrepancy between the oral and medical evidence. The courts found the delay in the FIR was satisfactorily explained, and the conduct of the informant was consistent with her role as a witness. The absence of an independent witness was attributed to the family dispute, and the courts did not find any discrepancy between the ocular and medical evidence.
